thread:
Kofi: Follow-up on postmortem for cascading cold-starts. We have repeated incidents where autoscaler oscillation + uneven cache warming leads to a handful of nodes getting overloaded. Need a dedicated 'when autoscaler flaps' subsection in the runbook with clear commands and an emergency contact path.

Leah: I'll take the subsection for 'Autoscaler-flap triage'. Add a step to check HPA events, recent scale decisions and steady-state desired vs actual replicas.

Tom: Include a quick one-liner to fetch the last 30 HPA events and the recent metrics: 

Tom: ```
# HPA events + last 5 scale decisions
kubectl -n infra get hpa inference -o yaml | yq '.status' && kubectl -n infra get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=inference -o tail -n 30
```

Hana: Put a note: if HPA has flapped more than 3 times in 10m, escalate to eng-sre and consider applying hold-on scaling annotation for 10m.

Incident Bot: Postmortem uploaded: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/cascading-coldstarts-206614 (sha: f7g8h9).

Kofi: Owners and deadlines:
- Leah: PR adding 'Autoscaler-flap' subsection + HPA commands  24h.
- Tom: diagnostic one-liners + small script  48h.
- Hana: escalation text and phone tree  72h.

Leah: Also suggest adding a canary scaling test in the runbook (how to run it on dev). I'll add steps and a checklist.

Tom: I'll include rollback commands and an example of how to re-enable autoscaler.

Kofi: Thanks. Please post PR links here when ready so we can mark the follow-ups done.
